citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
basis: The motel holds one merchant account, and the merchant agreement requires PCI DSS compliance and yearly validation. About 13,800 card transactions a year are taken at the front desk, by phone, from crew forms, through OTA virtual cards and on the booking engine. PCI SSC sets no size tiers; merchant levels are set by the card brands and were not verified, so no level is stated. The SAQ type follows the payment design and is decided in P03

obligation: FTC Act Section 5, with the FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees
basis: For-profit LLC; no size threshold. Part 464 covers short-term lodging 'at a hotel, motel, inn' (464.1) and businesses that offer services in physical locations as well as online. The motel charges a mandatory $6 nightly fee, shows rates on a roadside sign, a website, by phone, on its booking engine and through 3 OTAs, and publishes a privacy statement on its website
The motel obtains background-check reports on front desk and night audit applicants for a business purpose and keeps them on paper

obligation: State breach notification laws, with Florida as the worked example
basis: The PMS holds guest names with driver license and ID card numbers, and card numbers with security codes are kept in email and on paper. Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(g) includes these in personal information; 501.171(2) and (8) require reasonable security and disposal; 501.171(3) to (6) set notice duties. Most transient guests and many crew members live outside Florida, so the law of each state where affected individuals reside applies
No Illinois operations or employees and no biometric collection: the time clock uses PINs and the CCTV has no facial recognition

Not a final rule. The proposed size criterion (226.2(a)) reaches only entities above the SBA size standard, and the motel's revenue of about $1.1 million is far below the $40.0 million standard for NAICS 721110 (13 CFR 121.201)
The motel is a transient public lodging establishment and keeps its guest register electronically in the PMS. Registers more than 2 years old need not be made available to the division

obligation: Unconscionable prices during a declared state of emergency
basis: The dynamic pricing tool publishes room rates automatically, and the motel's county is inside the declared area in most statewide emergency declarations. The statute does not name motels; Chapter 509 treats occupancy of a motel unit as occupancy of a dwelling unit (509.013(12)), so the motel treats its room rates as covered (the cautious reading; counsel to confirm)

obligation: Merchant agreement: notice of a suspected compromise
basis: Notice to the acquirer within 24 hours of a suspected compromise of card data
Notice through the 24x7 breach hotline; use of the panel breach counsel and forensic firm
The largest crew client asks how its corporate card data and crew rosters are protected and disposed of, and accepts a self-assessment with a remediation plan. Not a legal duty

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule and Red Flags Rule
basis: No consumer credit is extended; the 2 crew companies that are invoiced are business accounts
No California business; revenue far below its thresholds

A controller must exceed $1 billion in global gross annual revenue and meet one of three further tests (50% or more of revenue from online advertising, a smart speaker and voice command service, or an app store with at least 250,000 applications). The motel's revenue is about $1.1 million and it meets none
Not a covered entity: the motel provides lodging, not health care, and is not a health plan or clearinghouse
Privately held LLC with no registered securities

Claims about algorithmic pricing in lodging have turned on whether competitors' non-public data are pooled in a shared tool. The motel subscribes to a dynamic pricing tool; its subscription terms are reviewed in P10
